sanskrit: śraddhayāgniḥ sam idhyate śraddhayā hūyate haviḥ | śraddhām bhagasya mūrdhani vacasā vedayāmasi ||
english: By Śraddhā (Faith) Agni is kindled; by Śraddhā the oblation is offered. I proclaim Śraddhā at the head of Bhaga (the Bountiful Lord), with my voice.

sanskrit: priyaṃ śraddhe dadataḥ priyaṃ śraddhe didāsataḥ | priyam bhojeṣu yajvasv idam ma uditaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: O Śraddhā, make dear the one who gives; make dear the one who desires to give. Make this utterance of mine dear among the generous and among the sacrificers.

sanskrit: yathā devā asureṣu śraddhām ugreṣu cakrire | evam bhojeṣu yajvasv asmākam uditaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: Just as the gods placed Śraddhā in the Asuras and in the mighty ones, so make our utterance dear among the generous and among the sacrificers.

sanskrit: śraddhāṃ devā yajamānā vāyugopā upāsate | śraddhāṃ hṛdayyayākūtyā śraddhayā vindate vasu ||
english: The gods and the worshippers, guarded by Vāyu, attend upon Śraddhā. By Śraddhā, by the sincere resolve of the heart, one obtains riches.

sanskrit: śraddhām prātar havāmahe śraddhām madhyaṃdinam pari | śraddhāṃ sūryasya nimruci śraddhe śrad dhāpayeha naḥ ||
english: Śraddhā we invoke in the morning; Śraddhā we invoke at midday; Śraddhā we invoke at the setting of the sun. O Śraddhā, cause us to have faith here.

sanskrit: śāsa itthā mahāṃ asy amitrakhādo adbhutaḥ | na yasya hanyate sakhā na jīyate kadā cana ||
english: Thus command, thou who art great, the miraculous devourer of enemies. He whose friend is never slain and never in any way overcome.

sanskrit: svastidā viśas patir vṛtrahā vimṛdho vaśī | vṛṣendraḥ pura etu naḥ somapā abhayaṃkaraḥ ||
english: May Indra, the lord of the people, the giver of welfare, the slayer of Vṛtra, the subduer of enemies, the mighty bull, the drinker of soma, the bestower of fearlessness, go before us.

sanskrit: vi rakṣo vi mṛdho jahi vi vṛtrasya hanū ruja | vi manyum indra vṛtrahann amitrasya abhidāsataḥ ||
english: Drive away the Rakṣas; drive away the oppressors; smash the jaws of Vṛtra. Drive away, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, the wrath of the enemy who attacks us.

sanskrit: vi na indra mṛdho jahi nīcā yaccha pṛtanyataḥ | yo asmāṃ abhidāsaty adharaṃ gamayā tamaḥ ||
english: Drive away our oppressors, O Indra; press down the assailants. He who attacks us — send him down to the lower darkness.

sanskrit: apendra dviṣato mano 'pa jijyāsato vadham | vi manyoḥ śarma yaccha varīyo yavayā vadham ||
english: Drive away, O Indra, the mind of the hater; drive away the blow of him who seeks to overcome us. Grant the shelter of thy grace; keep away the weapon afar.

sanskrit: īṅkhayantīr apasyuva indraṃ jātam upāsate | bhejānāsaḥ suvīryam ||
english: They who are active, swinging, attend on newly-born Indra; they have attained heroic strength.

sanskrit: tvam indra balād adhi sahaso jāta ojasaḥ | tvaṃ vṛṣan vṛṣed asi ||
english: Thou, O Indra, wast born with surpassing strength, from might and vigour. Thou, O bull, art indeed the bull.

sanskrit: tvam indrāsi vṛtrahā vy antrikṣam atiraḥ | ud dyām astabhnā ojasā ||
english: Thou, O Indra, art the slayer of Vṛtra; thou didst extend the atmosphere apart. With thy might thou didst prop up the sky.

sanskrit: tvam indra sajoṣasam arkam bibharṣi bāhvoḥ | vajraṃ śiśāna ojasā ||
english: Thou, O Indra, bearest in thy arms the hymn along with the dawn, whetting the vajra with thy might.

sanskrit: tvam indrābhibhūr asi viśvā jātāny ojasā | sa viśvā bhuva ābhavaḥ ||
english: Thou, O Indra, art the overpowerer of all beings with thy might. Thou hast become the lord over all existing things.

sanskrit: soma ekebhyaḥ pavate ghṛtam eka upāsate | yebhyo madhu pradhāvati tāṃś cid evāpi gacchatāt ||
english: For some Soma flows purified; for others ghee is attended upon; for those for whom honey streams forth — to them verily may this one (the deceased) go.

sanskrit: tapasā ye anādhṛṣyās tapasā ye svar yayuḥ | tapo ye cakrire mahas tāṃś cid evāpi gacchatāt ||
english: Those who by austerity are invincible, those who by austerity have gone to heaven, those who have made great austerity — to them verily may this one go.

sanskrit: ye yudhyante pradhaneu śūrāso ye tanūtyajaḥ | ye vā sahasradakṣiṇās tāṃś cid evāpi gacchatāt ||
english: The heroes who fight in battles, who give up their bodies, or those who bestow a thousand sacrificial fees — to them verily may this one go.

sanskrit: ye cit pūrva ṛtasāpa ṛtāvāna ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | pitṝn tapasvatoYama tāṃś cid evāpi gacchatāt ||
english: Those who first of all served the cosmic order, the guardians of ṛta, the promoters of ṛta — O Yama, send this one to those ascetic Fathers; to them verily may this one go.

sanskrit: sahasraṇīthāḥ kavayo ye gopāyanti sūryam | ṛṣīn tapasvatoYama tapojāṃ api gacchatāt ||
english: Those seers of a thousand paths who guard the sun — O Yama, may this one go to those ascetic ṛṣis, to those born of tapas.

sanskrit: arāyi kāṇe vikaṭe giriṃ gaccha sadānve | śirimbiṭhasya satvabhi tebhiṣ ṭvā cātayāmasi ||
english: O one-eyed, disfigured Arāyī (niggardly demon), go to the mountain without a path. With the warriors of Śirimbiṭha do we drive thee away.

sanskrit: catto itaś cattāmutaḥ sarvā bhrūṇāny āruṣī | arāyyam brahmaṇas pate tīkṣṇaśṛṇgodṛṣann ihi ||
english: Driven hence and driven thence, O red one who destroys all embryos — O Lord of prayer (Bṛhaspati), come here with sharp horns, looking at the Arāyī (niggardly demoness).

sanskrit: ado yad dāru plavate sindhoḥ pāre apūruṣam | tad ā rabhasva durhaṇo tena gaccha parastaram ||
english: That piece of timber which floats yonder on the other bank of the river, uninhabited by men — seize it, O evil-natured one; with it cross over to the farther shore.

sanskrit: yad dha prācīr ajagantoro maṇḍūradhāṇikīḥ | hatā indrasya śatavaḥ sarve budbudayāśavaḥ ||
english: Those who came from the east, the maṇḍūradhāṇikīḥ (dealers in iron-rust), all the enemies of Indra were slain, swift as bubbles.

sanskrit: parī me gām aneṣata pary agnim ahṛṣata | deveṣv akrata śravaḥ ka imāṃ ā dadharsati ||
english: They have led the cow around me; they have carried the fire around; among the gods they have won fame. Who now shall dare attack this woman?

sanskrit: agniṃ hinvantu no dhiyaḥ saptim āśum ivājiṣu | tena jeṣma dhanaṃ-dhanam ||
english: Let our prayers urge Agni on like a swift horse in the races; by him may we win wealth upon wealth.

sanskrit: yayā gā ākarāmahe senayāgne tavotā | tāṃ no hinva maghattaye ||
english: O Agni, by that army of thine, under thy protection, with which we have gathered cattle — urge that on for us to gain wealth.

sanskrit: āgne sthūraṃ rayim bhara pṛthuṃ gomantam aśvinam | aṃdhi khaṃ vartayā paṇim ||
english: O Agni, bring us abundant, wide-spreading wealth, rich in cattle and in horses; fill the well; turn away the Paṇi (miser).

sanskrit: agne nakṣatram ajaram ā sūryaṃ rohayo divi | dadhaj jyotir janebhyaḥ ||
english: O Agni, cause the ageless star, the sun, to rise in the sky, bearing light for mankind.

sanskrit: agne ketur viśām asi preṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭha upasthasat | bodhā stotre vayo dadhat ||
english: O Agni, thou art the banner of the clans; thou art the most beloved, the best who is present. Be aware of the singer; grant him vigour.

sanskrit: imā nu kam bhuvanā sīṣadhāmendraś ca viśve ca devāḥ ||
english: May Indra and all the gods now fulfil these worlds for us.

sanskrit: yajñaṃ ca nas tanvaṃ ca prajāṃ cādityair indraḥ saha cīkḷpāti ||
english: May Indra together with the Ādityas arrange for us the sacrifice, our bodies, and our progeny.

sanskrit: ādityair indraḥ sagaṇo marudbhir asmākam bhūtv avitā tanūnām ||
english: May Indra, together with the Ādityas and in company with the Maruts, be the protector of our bodies.

sanskrit: hatvāya devā asurān yad āyan devā devatvam abhirakṣamāṇāḥ ||
english: When the gods came, having slain the Asuras, guarding their divine sovereignty —

sanskrit: pratyañcam arkam anayañ chacībhir ād it svadhām iṣirām pary apaśyan ||
english: — they brought back the sun-hymn (the light) with their powers; and thereupon they beheld the vigorous self-law (svadhā, the primordial order of the universe).

sanskrit: sūryo no divas pātu vāto antrikṣāt | agnir naḥ pārthivebhyaḥ ||
english: May the Sun protect us from the sky; may Vāyu (the Wind) protect us from the atmosphere; may Agni protect us from earthly dangers.

sanskrit: joṣā savitar yasya te haraḥ śataṃ savāṃ arhati | pāhi no didyutaḥ patantyāḥ ||
english: O Savitṛ, thy golden arm is worthy of a hundred impulsions (savā). Protect us from the falling lightning.

sanskrit: cakṣur no devaḥ savitā cakṣur na uta parvataḥ | cakṣur dhātā dadhātu naḥ ||
english: May the divine Savitṛ grant us sight; may the mountain grant us sight; may Dhātṛ (the Creator) bestow sight upon us.

sanskrit: cakṣur no dhehi cakṣuṣe cakṣur vikhyai tanūbhyaḥ | saṃ cedaṃ vi ca paśyema ||
english: Grant us sight for the sake of seeing; grant us sight for beholding, for our bodies. May we together look out and see around us.

sanskrit: susaṃdṛśaṃ tvā vayam prati paśyema sūrya | vi paśyema nṛcakṣasaḥ ||
english: May we look upon thee, O Sūrya, beautiful in appearance. May we behold thee, endowed with vision like men.

sanskrit: ud asau sūryo agād ud ayam māmako bhagaḥ | ahaṃ tad vidvalā patim abhy asākṣi viṣāsahiḥ ||
english: Yonder sun has risen; this my good fortune (bhaga) has risen. I, who am wise and ever-victorious, have overcome my husband entirely.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ketur aham mūrdhāham ugrā vivācanī | mamed anu kratum patiḥ sehānāyā upācaret ||
english: I am the banner; I am the head; I am the powerful one who speaks out. My husband shall follow my will; let him attend upon me who am victorious.

sanskrit: mama putrāḥ śatruhao 'tho me duhitā virāṭ | utāham asmi saṃjayā patyau me śloka uttamaḥ ||
english: My sons are slayers of enemies; my daughter is a ruling queen. I myself am all-conquering; and my praise is supreme among my husband's people.

sanskrit: yenendro haviṣā kṛtvy abhavad dyumny uttamaḥ | idaṃ tad akri devā asapatnā kilābhuvam ||
english: With that oblation by which Indra performed his deed and became supremely resplendent — O gods, by that have I become free from rivals.

sanskrit: asapatnā sapatnaghnī jayanty abhibhūvarī | āvṛkṣam anyāsāṃ varco rādho astheyasām iva ||
english: Rival-free, slayer of rivals, victorious and overpowering — I have seized the lustre of those others as if seizing the wealth of those who offer nothing.

sanskrit: sam ajaiṣam imā ahaṃ sapatnīr abhibhūvarī | yathāham asya vīrasya virājāni janasya ca ||
english: I have conquered these rivals of mine, I who am the overpowerer; so that I may reign supreme over this hero and over his people.

sanskrit: tīvrasyābhivayaso asya pāhi sarvarathā vi harī iha muñca | indra mā tvā yajamānāso anye ni rīraman tubhyam ime sutāsaḥ ||
english: Drink of this sharp and invigorating draught; release both thy bay horses here, O all-conquering one. Let not other worshippers turn thee away, O Indra; these soma-pressings are for thee.

sanskrit: tubhyaṃ sutās tubhyam u sotvāsas tvāṃ giraḥ śvātryā ā hvayanti | indraedam adya savanaṃ juṣāṇo viśvasya vidvāṃ iha pāhi somam ||
english: For thee are these pressed drinks; for thee too are the soma-pressings; the praises of the assembly call thee hither. O Indra, delighting in this pressing of today, knowing all things, drink the soma here.

sanskrit: ya uśatā manasā somam asmai sarvahṛdā devakāmaḥ sunoti | na gā indras tasya parā dadāti praśastam ic cārum asmai kṛṇoti ||
english: He who with eager mind, with whole heart, devoted to the gods, presses soma for Indra — his cattle Indra does not give away to another; he makes for him a praiseworthy and pleasing (outcome).

sanskrit: anuspaṣṭo bhavaty eṣo asya yo asmai revān na sunoti somam | nir aratnau maghavā taṃ dadhāti brahmadviṣo hanty anānudiṣṭaḥ ||
english: He is left to suffer who, though wealthy, does not press soma for Indra. The bountiful Indra lays him down in misfortune; he slays the hater of sacred prayer, himself unbidden.

sanskrit: aśvāyanto gavyanto vājayanto havāmahe tvopagantavā u | ābhūṣantas te sumatau navāyāṃ vayam indra tvā śunaṃ huvema ||
english: Desiring horses, desiring cattle, desiring booty, we call thee, that thou shouldst come to us. Seeking favour in thy new grace, may we call thee, O Indra, for happiness.
